  - button "Outline"
  - article:
    - heading "Tourism Package Prediction" [level=1]
    - 'link "Permalink: Tourism Package Prediction"':
      - /url: "#tourism-package-prediction"
    - paragraph:
      - text: An end-to-end MLOps project for
      - strong: Visit with Us
      - text: "that predicts whether a customer will purchase a Wellness Tourism Package. It follows the supplied learner template and examples: dataset registration, reproducible preparation, model tuning with MLflow tracking, a Streamlit prediction app, and a GitHub Actions pipeline."
    - paragraph:
      - text: The local project includes an executed notebook and HTML submission.
      - strong: This project has not been published to GitHub or deployed to a public app.
      - text: Actual repository, workflow-run, and deployment links and screenshots must be added after publication; none are fabricated.
    - heading "Project layout" [level=2]
    - 'link "Permalink: Project layout"':
      - /url: "#project-layout"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Use this
      - strong: Tourism Package Prediction directory as the GitHub repository root
      - text: . In particular,
      - code: .github/workflows/
      - text: must be at the repository root.
    - code: ". ├── .github/workflows/pipeline.yml ├── .streamlit/config.toml ├── requirements-dev.txt ├── README.md ├── Project-DESC.txt ├── Learner_Template_Notebook_AML_and_MLOps_Project.ipynb ├── Tourism_Package_Prediction_Completed.ipynb ├── Tourism_Package_Prediction_Completed.html ├── tourism.csv # Original supplied dataset ├── tests/ └── tourism_project/ ├── requirements.txt ├── data/ │ ├── tourism.csv # Registered repository input │ └── processed/ # Generated; passed as workflow artifact │ ├── Xtrain.csv │ ├── Xtest.csv │ ├── ytrain.csv │ ├── ytest.csv │ └── split_manifest.json ├── model_building/ │ ├── data_register.py │ ├── prep.py │ └── train.py ├── deployment/ │ ├── app.py │ ├── requirements.txt │ ├── model.joblib │ └── metadata.json ├── reports/ # Validation and model evaluation outputs └── mlruns/ # Local MLflow tracking; workflow artifact"
    - button "Copy code to clipboard"
    - paragraph: The supplied description, original CSV, and learner template are retained. Generated train/test splits and local MLflow records are excluded from Git; the fitted model, metadata, and reports are intentionally committed for serving and review.
    - heading "Prediction scope and data handling" [level=2]
    - 'link "Permalink: Prediction scope and data handling"':
      - /url: "#prediction-scope-and-data-handling"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The business objective is
      - strong: prediction before contacting a customer
      - text: ". The model therefore uses these 13 customer attributes:"
    - paragraph:
      - code: Age
      - text: ","
      - code: CityTier
      - text: ","
      - code: Occupation
      - text: ","
      - code: Gender
      - text: ","
      - code: NumberOfPersonVisiting
      - text: ","
      - code: PreferredPropertyStar
      - text: ","
      - code: MaritalStatus
      - text: ","
      - code: NumberOfTrips
      - text: ","
      - code: Passport
      - text: ","
      - code: OwnCar
      - text: ","
      - code: NumberOfChildrenVisiting
      - text: ","
      - code: Designation
      - text: ", and"
      - code: MonthlyIncome
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - code: CustomerID
      - text: and exported row indices are identifiers, so they are removed.
      - code: TypeofContact
      - text: ","
      - code: DurationOfPitch
      - text: ","
      - code: NumberOfFollowups
      - text: ","
      - code: ProductPitched
      - text: ", and"
      - code: PitchSatisfactionScore
      - text: describe a contact or sales interaction and are excluded from the predictive features. Using these after-contact fields would change the intended business use.
    - paragraph:
      - text: Registration validates the expected raw schema and binary
      - code: ProdTaken
      - text: target and records a data summary. Preparation applies deterministic text cleanup, including
      - code: Fe Male
      - text: →
      - code: Female
      - text: and
      - code: Free Lancer
      - text: →
      - code: Freelancer
      - text: .
      - code: Single
      - text: and
      - code: Unmarried
      - text: remain separate source categories. Missing predictor values are retained for imputers fitted inside the training pipeline.
    - paragraph:
      - text: Preparation removes 194 duplicate rows with identical pre-contact predictors and target, reducing the 4,128 raw rows to 3,934 unique labeled profiles. Identical predictors with conflicting targets cause preparation to stop for manual review. A stratified 80/20 split with
      - code: random_state=42
      - text: produces 3,147 training rows and 787 test rows; explicit checks verify zero profile overlap and unique training profiles. Because duplicates have already been removed, ordinary three-fold
      - code: StratifiedKFold
      - text: avoids duplicate-profile contamination. Learned imputation and categorical encoding are fitted separately within each training fold.
    - paragraph: "Model selection compares 20 hyperparameter configurations: four Decision Trees, eight Random Forests, and eight Gradient Boosting models. The winner maximizes training cross-validation average precision. Its decision threshold maximizes F2 on training out-of-fold predictions, which weights recall more heavily than precision. The threshold calculation reuses the three training folds after model selection; those out-of-fold results are selection diagnostics, not an unbiased nested-cross-validation performance estimate. The test holdout is used for the final evaluation and is excluded from model and threshold selection."
    - paragraph: The saved model payload contains the complete fitted preprocessing/model pipeline, the decision threshold, and the expected feature columns. The app builds a dataframe with this same schema and uses the stored threshold. A purchase score is a model estimate for prioritizing outreach; the historical dataset does not establish causal marketing impact or guarantee future conversion rates.
    - heading "Local evaluation results" [level=2]
    - 'link "Permalink: Local evaluation results"':
      - /url: "#local-evaluation-results"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The selected Random Forest achieved training cross-validation average precision
      - strong: "0.6470"
      - text: . At the training-selected threshold
      - strong: "0.185"
      - text: ", the held-out test results were:"

    - paragraph:
      - text: The highest-scored 20% corresponds to 158 of the 787 test customers. These ranking results describe the historical holdout; the threshold-based predictions prioritize recall and consequently include false positives. Detailed metrics, the confusion matrix, tuning results, and predictions are saved in
      - code: tourism_project/reports/
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The historical
      - code: ProdTaken
      - text: label records package uptake; it does not confirm a future purchase of this newly introduced Wellness Tourism Package. Production use requires temporal validation, drift monitoring, fairness assessment, and probability-calibration checks. In this dataset,
      - code: Designation
      - text: perfectly maps to
      - code: ProductPitched
      - text: ; confirm that designation is independently known before outreach and was not assigned during sales segmentation before relying on it operationally.
    - heading "Run locally" [level=2]
    - 'link "Permalink: Run locally"':
      - /url: "#run-locally"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Use
      - strong: Python 3.12
      - text: "for both training and deployment. From this directory:"
    - text: python3.12 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install --upgrade pip python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt python -m tourism_project.model_building.data_register python -m tourism_project.model_building.prep python -m tourism_project.model_building.train python -m pytest -q python -m streamlit run tourism_project/deployment/app.py
    - button "Copy code to clipboard"
    - paragraph: The dependencies for the training pipeline and app pin matching NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, and joblib versions. This matters because the app loads a serialized fitted scikit-learn pipeline. The serving environment excludes MLflow and notebook dependencies.
    - paragraph:
      - text: Training writes evaluation reports to
      - code: tourism_project/reports/
      - text: ", and MLflow records to"
      - code: tourism_project/mlruns/
      - text: . Each tuning candidate has a tracked parameter set and validation score; the best run includes the final parameters, evaluation metrics, and saved artifacts. Local file tracking works without an MLflow server, ngrok account, or access token.
    - paragraph: "To view the experiments in the optional MLflow UI, install the full package in the development environment and point it at the same store:"
    - text: python -m pip install mlflow==3.0.1 mlflow ui --backend-store-uri tourism_project/mlruns --port 5000
    - button "Copy code to clipboard"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Open
      - code: http://127.0.0.1:5000
      - text: . Installing the full UI package is optional; the automated training pipeline uses
      - code: mlflow-skinny
      - text: and retains all experiment records as an artifact.
    - heading "Notebook and HTML submission" [level=2]
    - 'link "Permalink: Notebook and HTML submission"':
      - /url: "#notebook-and-html-submission"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Open
      - code: Tourism_Package_Prediction_Completed.ipynb

    - paragraph: "To rerun and export the completed notebook in your local environment:"
    - text: python -m ipykernel install --user --name tourism-mlops --display-name "Python (Tourism MLOps)" jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute Tourism_Package_Prediction_Completed.ipynb --inplace --ExecutePreprocessor.kernel_name=tourism-mlops --ExecutePreprocessor.timeout=1800 jupyter nbconvert --to html Tourism_Package_Prediction_Completed.ipynb

    - heading "GitHub Actions" [level=2]
    - 'link "Permalink: GitHub Actions"':
      - /url: "#github-actions"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The workflow runs on pushes to
      - code: main
      - text: ", pull requests targeting"
      - code: main
      - text: ", and manual dispatch. It has three machine-learning jobs followed by a separate publication job:"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - strong: "Register and validate dataset:"
        - text: validate the repository CSV and upload the registered CSV and data summary.
      - listitem:
        - strong: "Clean data and create holdout split:"
        - text: download the registered input, prepare the data, and upload train/test splits and the split manifest.
      - listitem:
        - strong: "Tune, track, evaluate, and test:"
        - text: download the prepared splits, train with MLflow tracking, evaluate, run the tests, and upload the tested model and reports. Tracking records are retained separately.
      - listitem:
        - strong: "Commit tested model to main:"
        - text: runs only after successful training/tests on
        - code: main
        - text: ", outside pull requests. It downloads the tested artifact and commits the model, metadata, and reports with"
        - code: "[skip ci]"
        - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The first three jobs have read-only repository tokens, including on pull requests from the same repository. Only publication receives
      - code: "contents: write"
      - text: . Concurrency prevents overlapping runs for the same ref; publication checks that
      - code: main
      - text: still matches the source revision used for training. If newer work exists, the old model stays available as a workflow artifact and publication is skipped. The workflow never force-pushes over newer commits.
    - paragraph:
      - text: For a new repository, upload this directory including its hidden
      - code: .github
      - text: directory. Choose
      - code: main
      - text: as the default branch, enable GitHub Actions, and ensure repository or organization policies permit the publication job to use its requested write permission. Protected-branch rules may require an approved alternative publication process. The workflow needs no personal access token or cloud secret.
    - paragraph:
      - text: Once published, inspect the
      - strong: Actions
      - text: tab and confirm all jobs completed. Download the
      - code: trained-deployment
      - text: artifact for model/reports and the
      - code: mlflow-experiments
      - text: artifact for tracking records. The workflow trains and commits the serving files; connecting the repository to Streamlit Community Cloud is a separate one-time deployment step.
